title: Will we ever quantize the centers of mass of heavy systems? A case for a Heisenberg cut in quantum mechanics
summary: The quantum orthodoxy attests that all dynamical degrees of freedom should be quantized, including those associated with the centers of mass of composite/complex systems, such as protons/pebbles. By assuming that the centers of mass of protons/pebbles should be quantized, one implies the existence of a corresponding Fock space, since, according to the present lore, quantum mechanics is a consequence of quantum field theory.
